m: उत्-था (उद्-√ स्था, Pāṇ. viii, 4, 61; cf. उत्-तम्भ्, col. 1), P. Ā. (but not Ā. in the sense of ‘rising, standing up’, Pāṇ. i, 3, 24) -तिष्ठति, -ते (pf. -तस्थौ, aor. -अस्थात् &c.) to stand up, spring up, rise, raise one's self, set out, RV.; AV.; ŚBr.; Ragh.; Śak.; Bhag. &c.; to rise (from the dead), BhP.; to rise (from any occupation), leave off; to finish, AitBr.; ŚBr.; TāṇḍyaBr. &c.; to come forth, arise, appear, become visible, result; to spring, originate from, RV.; AV.; ŚBr.; TS.; MBh.; Kathās. &c.; to come in (as revenues), Śak.; to rise (for the performance of any action); to be active or brave; to make efforts, take pains with, strive for; to excel, MBh.; R. &c.: Caus. -थापयति (aor. 1. sg. उद्-अतिष्ठिपम्, AV. vii, 95, 2) to cause to stand up, raise, rouse, start, AV.; AitBr.; TBr.; ŚBr.; MBh.; Daś.; BhP. &c.; to set up, lift up, erect, Gobh.; MBh.; R.; Hit. &c.; to get out, Hit.; to drive out, send out, push out, AitBr. : Kathās.; BhP.; to excite; to produce, Ragh.; Sāh.; to arouse, awaken, raise to life, make alive, animate; to stir up, agitate, ŚBr.; KauṣUp.; Hariv.; R.; Kathās. &c.: Desid. -तिष्ठासति, to wish or intend to stand up, ŚBr. xi, 1, 6, 5; to intend to leave off (a sacrifice), Nyāyam.
a: उत्था — {c1c} P. [उद्-स्था] 1 To get up, stand, rise, raise oneself; उत्तिष्ठेत्प्रथमं चास्य Ms. 2. 194; R. 9. 59; Śi. 9. 39. --2 To get up from, leave, give up or cease from; अनशनादुत्तिष्ठति Pt. 4. --3 To rise, come up (as the sun &c.). --4 To rebound (as a ball); कराभिघातोत्थितकन्दुकेयं R. 16. 83. --5 To come forth, arise, spring or originate from, accrue from; ग्रा माच्छतमुत्तिष्ठति Mbh; यदुत्तिष्ठति वर्णेभ्यो नृपाण क्षयितत्फलं Ś. 2. 13; अन्यदमृतादुत्थितम् K. 136; उदतिष्ठन् प्रशंसावाचः Dk. 49 shouts of applause burst forth (were heard); N. 22. 44. --6 To rise, increase in strength or power, grow, (as an enemy, disease &c.); (Atm.) उत्तिष्ठमानस्तु परो नोपेक्ष्यः पथ्यमिच्छता Śi. 2. 10 (= Pt. 1. 234.) --7 To become animated, rise (from the dead); मृतेत्थिता Ku. 7. 4. --8 To be active or brave, rise up; हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ Bg. 2. 3, 37; Mv. 2; Pt. 3. 21. --9 To make efforts; take pains, strive, try; उत्तिष्ठमानं मित्रार्थे कस्त्वां न बहु मन्यते Bk. 8. 12; 20. 18; Mv. 4. 6; मुकावुत्तिष्ठते जनः Ki. 11. 13; उदस्थित क्रतौ Śi. 14. 17. --10 To excel, surpass. --Caus. (उत्थापयति) 1 To cause to stand up, raise, lift up: उत्थाप्यते ग्रावा H. 3. 42; R. 14. 59; raise or throw up (as dust); R. 7. 39. --2 To instigate, excite, rouse to action; त्वामुत्थापयति द्वयं Śi. 2. 57, 102; Kām. 5. 40; H. 3. 92; Dk. 107. --3 To arouse, awaken, raise to life, make alive; प्राणो हीदं सर्वमुत्थापयति Śat. Br. --4 To support, feed, aid; अत्र परिकरोत्थापितोऽ र्थांतरन्यासालंकारः Malli. on Ki. 8. 4.

s: strI, (utTAnAya hareH praboDanAya yA ekAdaSI । asyAM BagavAn kzIrodaSayAno nArAyaRaH yoganidrAM vihAya uttizWati .) kArttikaSuklEkAdaSI ॥ aTa vizRUtTAnam । tatra divase revatyantayuktAyAM dvAdaSyAm । rAtrO revatyantapAdayoge tu divAtftIyaBAge revatIyuktadvAdaSyAm । dvAdaSyAmfkzABAve ekAdaSIpraBftipOrRamAsyantAnyatamatiTO revatyantapAdayoge । tadaBAve kevalAyAM dvAdaSyAM sanDyAyAM vizRuM saMpUjya । o~ “mahendrarudrEraBinUyamAno BavAnfzirvvanditavandanIyaH । prAptA taveyaM kila kOmudAKyA jAgfzva jAgfzva ca lokanATa ॥ meGA gatA nirmmala eza candraH SAradyapuzpARi ca lokanATa । ahaM dadAnIti ca puRyahetorjAgfzva jAgfzva ca lokanATa” ॥ tataSca । “uttizWottizwa govinda tyaja nidrAM jagatpate । tvayA cotTIyamAnena utTitaM Buvanatrayam” ॥ iti paWet । iti kftyatattvam ॥
v: strI utTAnasya hareH nidrAtaHpraboDanasya kAlaH ekAdaSI । cAndrakArttikaSuklEkAdaSyAm । tatra kAla vyavasTA--ti॰ ta॰ raGunandanena darSitA yaTA mAtsye “Sete vizRuH sadAzAQe mAdre ca parivarttate । kArttike paribuDyeta Suklapakze harerdine” BavizyanAradIyayoH “mEtrAdyapAde svapitIha vizRurvEzRavyamaDye parivarttate ca । pOzRAvasAne ca surArihantA prabuDyate mAsacatuzwayena” Bavizye “niSi svApodivotTAnaM sanDyAyAM parivarttanam । anyatra pAdayoge'pi dvAdaSyAmeva kArayet” । anyatra svApAdivihitarAtryAdItarakAle daSamIpratipadoSca । “kintanmEtrAdyapAdena? daSamyaMSena yo divA । pOzRa SezeRa kintena? pratipadyaTayoniSi” । daSamyaMSena daSamyA aMSoyatra pAde tena । yaH patipadi vA prAptastena vA kim? । atra daSamIpratipadorvajanAt taditarEkAdaSyAdipaYcatiTizu mEtrAdinakzatrapAdaviSezalABe dvAdaSIM vinApi SayanAdiriti pratIyate । vacanAntaram “revatyanto yadA rAtrO dvAdaSyA ca samAyutaH । tadA vibuDyate vizRurdinAnte prApya revatIm” dinAnte triDAviBaktadina tftIyaBAge divotyAnamityanuroDAt । vizRuDarmmottare “vizRurdivA na svapiti ta ca rAtrO prabuDyate । dvAdaSyAmfkzasaMyoge pAdayogo na kAraRam । aprApte dvAdaSImfkze utyAnaSayane hareH । pAdayogena karttavye nAhorAvaM vicintayet varAhapurARam । “dvAdaSyAM sanDisamaye nakzatrARAmasamBave । ABAkAsitapakzezu SayanAvarttanAdikam” ABAkAnAm AzAQaBAdrakArttikAnAm । tataSca dvAdaSyAM niSAdO nakzatramAtrayogAt dvAdaSyAmfkzABAve tiTyantare niSAdyanAdareRa pAdaviSezayogAt, tadaBAve dbAdaSyAM sanDyAyAmeva SayanAdikaM boDanantu dvAdaSyAM rAtrO revatyantapAdayoge dinatftIyaBAga iti viSezaH” ।
m: उत्थानैकादशी f. the eleventh day in the light or former half of the month Kārttikā (when Viṣṇu rises from his sleep).
उत्थानीय mfn. belonging to the completion, forming the conclusion, TāṇḍyaBr. Comm. on Lāṭy.

Causing to arise or spring up. --नं 1 The act of rising or standing up, getting up; शनैर्यष्ट्युत्थानं Bh. 3. 9. --2 Rising (as of luminaries); इंदुं नवोत्थानमिवेंदुमत्यै R. 6. 31 newly risen. --3 Rise, origin. --4 Resurrection. --5 (a) Effort, exertion, activity; मेदश्छेदकृशोदरं लघु भवत्युत्थानयोग्यं वपुः Ś. 2. 5; ˚शीलः Dk. 153 disposed to work; Mv. 6. 23; यद्युत्थानं भवेत्सह Ms. 9. 215, effort (for money), acquisition of property. (b) Manly exertion, manhood. --6 Energy. --7 Joy, pleasure. --8 War, battle. --9 An army. --10 Evacuating (by stool &c.). --11 A book. --12 A court yard. --13 A shed where sacrifices are offered. --14 A term, limit, boundary. --15 Business (cares &c.) of a family or realm. --16 Reflection. --17 Proximate cause of a disease. --18 Awakening. --Comp. --एकादशी the eleventh day in the light fortnight of Kārttika when Viṣṇu rises from his four months' sleep (also called प्रबोधिनी).
